text:
alex: heads up — rolling FP8 on H100/L40S. saw a reproducible perf regression on L40S with long contexts (4k). kv cache hit-rate dropped ~15% and p95/token jumped. attaching quick profile below

maria: can you paste the profile and the transformer_engine config you used?

alex: here you go — baseline run on L40S, seq=4096, fp8 enabled, default kernel selector
```text
profile:
  model: redwood-v1
  hw: L40S
  seq: 4096
  mode: fp8
  kernel: te_fp8_gemm_v2
  tokens/s: 320
  avg_ms/token: 12.3
  p95_ms/token: 48.1
  kv_cache_hit: 84.7%
  kernel_switches: 3
  fallbacks_to_int8: 6%
  kv_evictions_per_min: 42
  observed_batch_window_ms: 6
```

lee: that kv_evictions_per_min looks high for 4k. are you using prefetching? what eviction policy?

alex: default prefetch 4, eviction=lru. transformer_engine config snippet:
```yaml
transformer_engine:
  fp8_enabled: true
  kernel_selector:
    prefer: fp8
    fallback_threshold_ms: 30  # switch to int8 if kernel latency > 30ms
    max_kernel_switches: 2
  kv:
    prefetch_next_n: 4
    eviction_policy: lru
    max_cache_size_mb: 8192
  batching:
    mode: continuous
    max_batch: 128
    batch_window_ms: 8
```

sam: quick suggestion: try forcing max_kernel_switches=1 and lower fallback_threshold_ms to 20, increase prefetch_next_n to 12. also run with --batching=continuous --max-batch=64 and capture kernel_scheduler traces. maybe kernel handoffs + small batch window are thrashing kv locality. :thinking: 

alex: ran that variant (flags above). new numbers:
```text
variant A:
  prefetch_next_n: 12
  fallback_threshold_ms: 20
  max_kernel_switches: 1
  batch_window_ms: 10
  tokens/s: 360
  avg_ms/token: 10.8
  p95_ms/token: 36.9
  kv_cache_hit: 90.2%
  kv_evictions_per_min: 18
  kernel_switches: 1
  fallbacks_to_int8: 1%
```

lee: nice improvement on throughput and hits. p95 still higher than H100 but acceptable. do you have kernel_scheduler trace snippet?

alex: attached excerpt — kernel_selector was flipping between te_fp8_gemm_v2 and te_fp8_gemm_slowpath when sequence growth > 2k; scheduler forced smaller micro-batches which triggered early kv eviction. short excerpt:
```text
[scheduler] pick: te_fp8_gemm_v2 (lat 12ms)
[scheduler] observe: tail_latency spike -> fallback to te_fp8_gemm_slowpath
[scheduler] switch_count++ -> cache eviction triggered by increased per-request mem churn
```

maria: sounds like a coupling between kernel selection heuristics and kv eviction thresholds. two immediate mitigations: 1) bias kernel_selector to prefer stable fp8 microkernels on L40S when seq > 1024 (deprioritize slowpath), 2) increase kv prefetch and reduce eviction aggressiveness for warmup window. also run calibration with representative long-context prompts (fp8 calibration can shift dynamic ranges).

alex: agreed. short-term action items I ran and will push to canary: lower fallback_threshold_ms->20, max_kernel_switches->1, prefetch_next_n->12, batch_window_ms->10. long-term: we should add a kernel_selector signal that considers kv_cache_hit_rate and not just raw kernel latency. filing follow-up ticket. @maria @lee

perf-bot: canary perf job queued (#3217) — collecting traces and kv metrics, ETA ~15m
